mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a property of a many‑one function f:A\rightarrow B?

options.A: At least two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
options.B: No two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
options.C: Some elements of B may have no pre‑image in A.
options.D: The function may also be onto.

mcqs.answer: No two distinct elements of A have the same image in B.
mcqs.explanation: A many‑one function allows two or more different domain elements to map to the same codomain element, so statement B (which says the opposite) is false. Statements A, C and D can all be true for a many‑one function. Hence B is the only incorrect property.

mcqs.question: Let A={1,2,3} and B={a,b,c,d}. Define f:A\rightarrow B by f(1)=a, f(2)=b, f(3)=c. Which statement is correct?
mcqs.explanation: An into function does not cover every element of the codomain. Since element d in B has no pre‑image, f is not onto; it is a valid function and is into. Therefore option B is correct, while A and C are false and D is incorrect because the mapping satisfies the definition of a function.

mcqs.question: Let f:{1,2,3}\rightarrow{a,b,c} be defined by f(1)=a, f(2)=b, f(3)=c and let g:{1,2,3}\rightarrow{a,b,c} be defined by g(1)=a, g(2)=a, g(3)=b. Which statement correctly compares the two functions with respect to being onto?

options.A: Both f and g are onto
options.B: f is onto but g is not onto
options.C: g is onto but f is not onto
options.D: Neither f nor g is onto

mcqs.answer: f is onto but g is not onto
mcqs.explanation: A function is onto (surjective) if every element of the codomain has at least one pre‑image. In f, each of a, b, c is hit, so f is onto. In g, element c has no pre‑image, so g is not onto. Hence option B correctly describes the situation.

mcqs.question: Which of the following functions f:\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R} is bijective?
mcqs.explanation: A bijective function must be both one‑to‑one and onto. f(x)=x^{3} is strictly increasing over all real numbers, giving a unique output for each input (one‑to‑one) and covering every real number (onto). f(x)=x^{2} is not one‑to‑one, e^{x} is not onto \mathbb{R} (its range is (0,\infty)), and \sin x is not one‑to‑one nor onto \mathbb{R}. Thus option C is the only bijective function.
